pages.body:
Why This Book Exists


Have you ever been to a really old festival? Maybe a harvest festival. Maybe a New Year celebration. Maybe a religious holiday that your grandparents celebrated. It felt old. It felt deep. It felt like there was a story underneath the story.


The Old Testament is full of festivals. There are seven major ones. They involve trumpets and tents. They involve fasting and feasting. They involve blood and fire. On the surface they look like ancient cultural traditions. But they are not. They are a calendar. They are a prophetic calendar. Every festival was a shadow of something coming. Every celebration was a rehearsal for a reality.


This book is for the curious. It is for the spiritual seeker who senses there is more. It is for the person who wants to understand why ancient rituals still matter today. Over the next 30 days, we are going to look at 30 ancient rituals and festivals. We are going to decode them. We are going to see what they were really pointing to. And we are going to discover that every single one of them points to Jesus.


The Value You Will Get


By the end of this book, you will not see the Old Testament as a list of outdated rules. You will see it as a divine calendar. You will understand why the Passover matters. You will understand what the Feast of Trumpets was really about. You will see the hidden pattern. And you will have a new lens to read the Bible. A lens that reveals Jesus in every festival.


How to Use This Guide


This is a 30 day journey. Each day takes about 10 minutes. Read the hook. Read the ancient text. Read the fulfillment. Read the verdict. Read the resonance. Read the prayer. If you are not sure how to pray, just read the words out loud. God hears honest words. He is not looking for fancy...

pages.body:
The Hook
Imagine a dinner party that saved a nation. Imagine a meal so important that it is still celebrated after thousands of years. Imagine a night so significant that it is woven into the identity of millions of people. That is Passover.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"This is a day you are to commemorate; for the generations to come you shall celebrate it as a festival to the LORD—a lasting ordinance." - Exodus 12:14 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Israelites were slaves in Egypt. They cried out to God. God sent Moses. God sent plagues. The final plague was the death of the firstborn. But God gave a way out. Each family was told to kill a lamb. They were told to paint the lamb's blood on the doorposts of their houses. When the angel of death passed through Egypt, it would see the blood. It would pass over that house. The people inside would live. This is the Passover. It is a festival of deliverance.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed." - 1 Corinthians 5:7


Jesus is the Passover Lamb. He died on the cross. His blood was shed. His blood was painted on the doorposts of our hearts. When judgment comes, it passes over us. We are saved by His blood. The festival of Passover was a rehearsal. The reality is Jesus.


The Verdict
The Passover was a specific event. The lamb had to be perfect. Its blood had to be applied. The pattern is precise. The prophecy is perfect. The shadow is clear. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
The blood of the Passover lamb saved a nation. The blood of Jesus saves the world. Are you covered by the blood?


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my Passover Lamb. Thank you for shedding your blood for me. Thank you that the judgment has passed over me because of you. I am safe because of you. Amen.

The Hook
Why did God care about a baking ingredient? Why did He tell the Israelites to remove all yeast from their homes? It seems like a small thing. It seems like a weird detail. But it is a shadow. It is a clue. It points to something deeper.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread, because it was on this very day that I brought your divisions out of Egypt." - Exodus 12:17 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


When the Israelites left Egypt, they had to leave quickly. They did not have time to let their bread rise. They baked unleavened bread. It was flat. It was hard. It was the bread of haste. But God told them to keep celebrating this festival. For seven days every year, they were to remove all yeast from their homes. Yeast was a symbol of sin. It spreads. It puffs up. It was a reminder to live a holy life.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Therefore let us keep the Festival, not with the old bread leavened with malice and wickedness, but with the bread of sincerity and truth." - 1 Corinthians 5:8


Paul applies this to Jesus. He says we are to remove the yeast of sin from our lives. We are to live with sincerity and truth. Jesus is the Bread of Life. He is the unleavened bread. He is without sin. If we want to live like Him, we must remove the yeast.


The Verdict
This is a shadow about sanctification. It is about a life that is set apart. God cares about the small things. He cares about the hidden things. He cares about the yeast. If God cares about yeast, He cares about the small things in your life.


The Resonance
What is the yeast in your life? What is the thing that puffs you up? What is the thing that spreads? God is asking you to remove it.


The Prayer
God, help me to remove the yeast from my life. Help me to stop tolerating the things that separate me from you. Give me a heart of sincerity and truth. Help me to live a holy life. Amen.

The Hook
Have you ever given someone your first paycheck? There is something special about the first. It is the best. It is the earliest. God asked the Israelites to give Him their firstfruits. He asked for the first. This is a shadow of resurrection.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God." - Exodus 23:19 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The firstfruits was an offering. It was the first sheaf of the harvest. The Israelites were told to bring it to God. It was a sign of trust. It showed they believed God would provide the rest. But it was also a shadow. The firstfruits was a promise that a greater harvest was coming.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep." - 1 Corinthians 15:20


Jesus is the firstfruits. He is the first to rise from the dead. His resurrection is a promise that we too will rise. If the firstfruits is raised, the rest will be raised too. This is the hope of the Christian faith.


The Verdict
The firstfruits was a shadow. It pointed to a resurrection. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you believe in the resurrection? If He rose, then the rest will rise. The firstfruits is a promise. The harvest is coming.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for rising from the dead. Thank you for being the firstfruits. Thank you for the promise that we will rise too. Thank you for the hope of eternal life. Amen.

The Hook
Fifty days after Passover, there was another festival. It was called the Feast of Weeks. It was also called Pentecost. It was a harvest festival. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Count off seven weeks from the time you begin to put the sickle to the standing grain. Then celebrate the Festival of Weeks to the LORD your God by giving a freewill offering in proportion to the blessings the LORD your God has given you." - Deuteronomy 16:9-10 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Feast of Weeks was a celebration of the wheat harvest. The people brought their firstfruits. They brought a freewill offering. They rejoiced before the Lord. It was a time of gratitude. It was a time of joy. It was a shadow. It pointed to a greater harvest. It pointed to a greater outpouring.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"When the day of Pentecost came, they were all together in one place. Suddenly a sound like the blowing of a violent wind came from heaven and filled the whole house where they were sitting." - Acts 2:1-2


The Feast of Weeks was fulfilled on the day of Pentecost. The Holy Spirit was poured out on the disciples. The church was born. The harvest began. The freewill offering was not wheat. It was people. It was a harvest of souls. It was a shadow that became a reality.


The Verdict
The Feast of Weeks was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to the Holy Spirit. It pointed to Pentecost. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is the Spirit.


The Resonance
Do you want to be part of the harvest? Do you want to be filled with the Spirit? The Feast of Weeks is a reminder that God pours out His Spirit on those who seek Him.


The Prayer
Holy Spirit, thank you for being poured out on the day of Pentecost. Thank you for the harvest of souls. Fill me with your presence. Use me in your harvest. Amen.

Jesus is the trumpet call. He will come down from heaven with a loud command. The trumpet will sound. The dead in Christ will rise. We will be gathered to Him. The Feast of Trumpets was a rehearsal. The reality is the return of Jesus.

The Hook
The Day of Atonement was the holiest day of the year. It was a day of fasting. It was a day of sacrifice. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"This is to be a lasting ordinance for you: On the tenth day of the seventh month you must deny yourselves and not do any work—whether native-born or a foreigner residing among you—because on this day atonement will be made for you, to cleanse you." - Leviticus 16:29-30 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Day of Atonement was a day of national cleansing. The high priest entered the Most Holy Place. He offered sacrifices for his own sin. He offered sacrifices for the sin of the people. The blood was sprinkled on the mercy seat. The people fasted. They denied themselves. They waited. It was a shadow. It pointed to a greater sacrifice. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"He did not enter by means of the blood of goats and calves; but he entered the Most Holy Place once for all by his own blood, thus obtaining eternal redemption." - Hebrews 9:12


Jesus is the Day of Atonement. He is the high priest. He is the sacrifice. He entered the Most Holy Place once for all. He obtained eternal redemption. The Day of Atonement was a rehearsal. The reality is the cross.


The Verdict
The Day of Atonement was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you need atonement? Do you need cleansing? The Day of Atonement is a reminder that Jesus made atonement for you. Once. For all.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my Day of Atonement. Thank you for entering the Most Holy Place. Thank you for obtaining eternal redemption. Thank you for cleansing me. Amen.

Jesus is the Feast of Tabernacles. He is the dwelling place of God. He is the glory. He is the presence. He is the fulfillment of the feast. He came to dwell among us. He came to be with us. He came to live in us.


The Verdict

The Hook
The Year of Jubilee was a once-in-fifty-years event. It was a reset button. It was a shadow of something greater.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee for you; each of you is to return to your family property and to your own clan." - Leviticus 25:10 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The Year of Jubilee was a year of freedom. It was a year of release. It was a year of restoration. Every fifty years, the Israelites were to proclaim liberty. Slaves were set free. Debts were cancelled. Land was returned. It was a reset. It was a fresh start. It was a shadow. It pointed to a freedom that would come. It pointed to Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim freedom for the prisoners and recovery of sight for the blind, to set the oppressed free, to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor." - Luke 4:18-19


Jesus is the Jubilee. He is the freedom. He is the release. He is the restoration. He is the fulfillment of the Jubilee. He proclaims good news to the poor. He proclaims freedom to the prisoners. He sets the oppressed free.


The Verdict
The Jubilee was a shadow. It pointed to a person. It pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
Are you in bondage? Are you in debt? Remember the Jubilee. Remember Jesus. He is your freedom. He is your release. He is your fresh start.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my Jubilee. Thank you for proclaiming freedom to me. Thank you for releasing me from bondage. Help me to walk in your freedom. Amen.

The red heifer was a sacrifice for cleansing. The red heifer was taken outside the camp. It was killed. It was burned. Its ashes were collected. They were mixed with water. Jesus is the red heifer. He suffered outside the city gate. He was burned. He was the ultimate cleansing. His blood cleanses us. His blood purifies us. He is the fulfillment of the red heifer.

Jesus is the Feast of Purim. He is the deliverance. He is the rescue. He is the fulfillment of the feast. He rescued us from the dominion of darkness. He brought us into His kingdom. He is the greater deliverance.

The Hook
The rituals were shadows. The festivals were shadows. The tabernacle was a shadow. But the reality is Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"The law is only a shadow of the good things that are coming—not the realities themselves." - Hebrews 10:1 (Written around 60 A.D.)


The law was a shadow. It was a shadow of the good things that are coming. It was a shadow of the realities themselves. It was a shadow of Jesus. The rituals could not make perfect. The sacrifices could not make perfect. They were shadows. They were pointing to something greater. They were pointing to a person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"These are a shadow of the things that were to come; the reality, however, is found in Christ." - Colossians 2:17


Jesus is the reality. He is the substance. He is the fulfillment of the shadow. He is the good thing that is coming. He is the perfect one. He is the one who makes perfect. He is the one who completes the shadow.


The Verdict
The rituals were shadows. They pointed to a person. They pointed to Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance
You have the real thing. You have Jesus. You do not need to keep looking at shadows. You can live in the reality. You can live in the substance. You can live in Christ.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the reality. Thank you for being the substance. Thank you for being the fulfillment of the shadow. Help me to stop living in the shadow. Help me to live in the reality. Help me to live in you. Amen.



END MATTER


The 30-Day Festival Challenge
You have journeyed through 30 ancient rituals and festivals. Now what? I challenge you to read the book of Hebrews. It is 13 chapters. It is the perfect follow-up to this book. It will show you how Jesus is greater than the angels, greater than Moses, greater than the priests, and greater than the sacrifices. As you read, look for the shadows. Look for the substance. Look for Jesus.


A Note on Faith
The festivals are evidence. They are evidence of a divine plan. But evidence does not save you. The festivals point to a person. The festivals point to Jesus. You can understand the festivals and still miss the substance. The invitation is for your heart. Jesus said, "Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in." The festivals are on the table. The door is open. It is your choice.


About the Author
Christine A. writes for the spiritually curious. He is passionate about showing people the hidden wisdom of the Bible. He lives with his family and enjoys good coffee and long conversations with skeptics. He believes that honest questions deserve honest answers.

If you enjoyed this journey, the next book in the series goes deeper. The Substance Behind the Symbol takes a 30 day look at the ancient laws and how they reveal living grace. It is for the seeker who wants to go further.
